column1: Macroplastic flux measurements were taken in January and between May and October 2019, using the harmonized visual counting method described  by González-Fernández and Hanke, 2017 and van Emmerik et al., 2018. Measurements  were taken from a bridge for one day per week in Las Vacas and three days per week in Zacapa and Morales for about five hours by two persons. Given the height of the bridge and the flow speed of the river, objects smaller than 2 cm are difficult to observe, and submerged objects are visible to a depth of 10 cm (depending on flow conditions). Therefore, not the all macroplastic items (> 0.5 cm) could be observed, and not all macroplastic transport over the full water column could be observed. At these locations, no tidal influence was observed in the river, and flow was always in downstream direction. The river was divided in fixed segments , depending on the width of the river (Table 1), assuring that the full cross section of the river is monitored, and in each segment plastic items were counted for three consecutive minutes. Measurements were taken between 5 AM and 3 PM, local time . Each segment was counted at least once per hour. The data for different segments and counting periods as processed to obtain daily average macroplastic fluxes for the full river width (average items per hour). First, the plastic flux over the full river width is calculated by a summation of items counted per segment, multiplied by time to cover the full hour. Segments that were counted once per hour (for three minutes) are multiplied by a factor 20 to obtain the segment flux per hour. If a segment was counted several times (for three minutes) in an hour, the average flux per three minutes is multiplied by a factor 20. Second, the average value of hourly fluxes in a day is calculated (daily average items per hour for full river width).
